Reference Guide

DeFi Glossary

80+ essential terms, concepts, and mechanisms that power decentralized finance — from Airdrop to ZK-Rollup.

80+
Terms
7
Categories
A–Z
Navigable
Popular Terms
AMM
Automated market maker — a decentralized exchange mechanism using liquidity pools instead of order books.
TVL
Total value locked — the aggregate amount of assets deposited in a DeFi protocol.
Impermanent Loss
Value gap between LP assets in a pool vs. holding them in a wallet.
APR vs APY
Simple annual rate vs. compound-adjusted annual yield — know the difference.
Liquidation
Forced closure of a collateralized loan when its health factor drops too low.
Flash Loan
Uncollateralized loan within a single transaction, reverted if not repaid.
A
General

Airdrop

Tokens distributed for free to wallet addresses, often as a reward for protocol usage, early adoption, or as a public good allocation. Airdrops are a common go-to-market strategy in DeFi.

Dashboard
Often used to bootstrap decentralised governance by distributing tokens widely to community members.
AMM

AMM Automated Market Maker

A DEX mechanism using mathematical pricing functions (typically x·y=k) and liquidity pools instead of traditional order books. Liquidity providers deposit token pairs; traders swap against them at prices determined algorithmically.

Curve Dashboard
Uniswap, Curve, and Balancer are popular AMMs. The pricing curve can be stable (for similar assets) or volatile (for unrelated pairs).
Risk

Anti-Griefing Mechanism

Protocol rules designed to prevent malicious actors from exploiting or harming other users — e.g., caps on liquidation bonuses, cooldown periods, or moral hazard safeguards.

Risk Dashboard
Prevents malicious liquidators from gaming liquidation thresholds to steal value from borrowers.
Lending

APR Annual Percentage Rate

The simple annual interest rate charged for borrowing or earned via lending — excludes compounding. APR is lower than APY for the same nominal rate when interest is compounded multiple times per year.

Aave Compound
If a protocol reports APR of 5%, paid monthly, the actual APY is ~5.12% because each month's interest earns interest in subsequent months.
Lending

APY Annual Percentage Yield

The effective annual yield including the effect of compounding interest over the measurement period. APY = (1 + r/n)n − 1 where n = compounding periods per year.

Aave Lido
A 5% APR compounded daily yields approximately 5.127% APY. Always compare APY when evaluating yield opportunities.
General

Authorization / Approval

An on-chain transaction where a user grants a smart contract permission to transfer a specific token on their behalf. Required once per token per spender (though many tokens use infinite approvals for UX convenience).

Dashboard
Revoking unused approvals regularly is a key security hygiene practice. Use a token approval explorer or revoke.cash to audit approvals.
B
MEV

Backrun

A bot or miner strategy that submits a transaction immediately after a large on-chain trade to profit from the price impact. Commonly seen after a big swap moves the price, allowing a backrunner to buy low and sell high in the next block.

MEV
Backrunning is one of the most common MEV strategies. It requires the bot to watch the mempool and submit within the same block after the target transaction.
AMM

Bonding Curve

A mathematical curve that defines the price of a token as a function of its circulating supply. As tokens are bought, price rises along the curve; as tokens are sold, price falls. Used by AMMs and some token distribution mechanisms.

Curve
Bonding curves can be linear, exponential, or custom. They enable continuous price discovery without an order book.
Bridges

Bridge

A protocol that locks tokens on one blockchain and mints equivalent wrapped tokens on another, enabling cross-chain asset transfers. Bridges can be trust-minimized (-liquidity pools, proof-of-stake) or trusted (custodial).

Bridges
Cross-chain bridges have suffered the largest DeFi exploits. Always verify bridge security models before transferring significant value.
C
Lending

CDP Collateral Debt Position

A smart contract vault where users lock collateral (e.g., ETH) to generate synthetic debt (e.g., DAI). MakerDAO pioneered this model. The position is automatically liquidated if collateral falls below the required ratio.

MakerDAO
Unlike traditional loans, CDPs don't have fixed repayment schedules — users can close their position at any time by repaying the generated stablecoin.
Lending

Collateral Factor

The maximum percentage of an asset's value that can be borrowed against it. If ETH has a 80% collateral factor, a user can borrow up to $800 worth of other assets for every $1,000 of ETH supplied.

Aave Compound
Higher collateral factors allow more leverage but increase liquidation risk. Assets with higher volatility typically have lower collateral factors.
Lending

Compound Interest

Interest earned on both the principal and previously accumulated interest. In DeFi, interest is typically accrued per Ethereum block or per second, compounding continuously rather than on a fixed schedule.

Compound Aave
The compounding frequency dramatically affects APY. Daily compounding on a 5% APR yields ~5.127% APY; per-second compounding yields ~5.127%. The difference is marginal at small rates but significant over time.
Staking

Convex Finance

A yield aggregator built on Curve that allows CRV stakers to earn boosted CRV rewards without actively managing positions. It simplifies Curve LPing and automatically compounds yields for users.

Curve
Users deposit their Curve LP tokens into Convex to receive cvxCRV, which auto-claims and re-stakes CRV rewards on behalf of LPs.
Staking

CRV Curve DAO Token

The governance token of the Curve Finance protocol. CRV holders stake it to vote on protocol parameters, gauge weights, and rewards allocation. Staked CRV (veCRV) provides additional governance power and fee claims.

Curve
CRV has a 3-month to 4-year lockup period for veCRV (vote-escrowed CRV). Longer locks receive higher boost multipliers.
D
Governance

DAO Decentralized Autonomous Organization

An on-chain organization governed by token holders who vote on proposals to allocate treasury, update protocol parameters, or upgrade smart contracts. DAOs replace traditional corporate structures with transparent, programmable governance.

Curve MakerDAO
MakerDAO, Curve DAO, and Aave DAO are among the largest DeFi treasuries, collectively controlling billions in assets through on-chain voting.
AMM

DEX Decentralized Exchange

A non-custodial exchange running on a blockchain via smart contracts, enabling direct token swaps without intermediaries. AMM DEXs (Uniswap, Curve) use liquidity pools; order-book DEXs use off-chain or on-chain order books.

Curve Aggregators
DEXs eliminate counterparty risk (you always control your funds) but introduce smart contract risk, impermanent loss, and slippage risk.
Governance

Distribution Model

The mechanism by which a protocol allocates its token supply — through liquidity mining, staking rewards, team allocations, or airdrops. The distribution model directly shapes long-term decentralization and governance quality.

Dashboard
Wide token distribution correlates with stronger censorship resistance and decentralisation. Protocols with concentrated team/VC allocations face higher governance capture risk.
General

DPI DeFi Pulse Index

A passive, rules-based index that tracks a basket of the largest DeFi tokens by market weight. Allows investors to gain diversified DeFi exposure without picking individual tokens.

Aggregators
DPI rebalances quarterly. Holdings include UNI, AAVE, MKR, COMP, SNX, and other top DeFi tokens proportional to float-adjusted market cap.
E
Staking

EigenLayer

A middleware protocol on Ethereum that enables restaking of ETH (or LSDs like stETH/rETH) to secure multiple parallel networks (AVSs) simultaneously, earning additional yield on already-staked capital.

EigenLayer Lido
Restakers opt into EigenLayer contracts and delegate stake to AVS operators. Slashing on any AVS can result in total stake slashing across all services.
Governance

Emission

The rate at which a DeFi protocol mints and distributes its native tokens as rewards to liquidity providers, stakers, or governance participants. Emission schedules can be fixed, decaying, or dynamic based on governance votes.

Dashboard
High emissions dilute existing token holders and are typically used as a bootstrapping incentive. Sustainable protocols eventually transition to fee-revenue-based incentives.
General

ERC-20

The Ethereum standard for fungible tokens. Defines a common interface for token transfers, balances, allowances, and supply. Every token on Ethereum (and EVM-compatible chains) that follows this standard is ERC-20 compatible.

Dashboard
Most DeFi tokens (USDT, USDC, DAI, UNI, AAVE) are ERC-20 tokens. Each has a contract address that uniquely identifies it on Ethereum.
General

ERC-4626 Tokenized Vault Standard

An Ethereum standard for tokenized yield-bearing vaults that extends ERC-20. Enables composable yield strategies — a single interface for deposits, withdrawals, share accounting, and yield accrual across any vault.

Aave Pendle
ERC-4626 dramatically improves interoperability between yield protocols and aggregators, reducing integration effort and audit surface.
Staking

ETH Staking

Depositing ETH into the Ethereum Beacon Chain as proof-of-stake validator collateral to secure the network and earn staking rewards (~4–5% APY as of 2024). Staked ETH is locked until future upgrades.

Lido EigenLayer
Stakers run validators that attest to blocks and earn rewards. Penalties (slashing) apply for downtime or malicious behaviour. Liquid staking tokens (LSTs) represent staked ETH for use in DeFi.
F
AMM

Fee Tier

The percentage of each swap that liquidity providers earn in a Uniswap V3 pool (0.05%, 0.30%, 1.00%, and custom tiers). Higher fee tiers compensate for higher price impact risk in volatile token pairs.

Curve Aggregators
Stable asset pairs (USDC/USDT) typically use 0.05% or 0.01% tiers. Volatile pairs (ETH/MKR) use 0.30% or higher.
MEV

Flash Loan

An uncollateralized loan executed entirely within one blockchain transaction. The assets must be borrowed and returned (plus fees) within the same block or the entire transaction reverts — no collateral required.

MEV Aave
Flash loans enable complex arbitrage, collateral swaps, and self-liquidation strategies — all without upfront capital. They're a key enabler of DeFi composability but also power exploit vectors.
General

Fren

A term of endearment in crypto culture meaning "friend." Used in CT (Crypto Twitter) and Discord to address fellow community members or people you've interacted with online. DeFi is social — fren is how we address each other.

Dashboard
Originated from the Pobble frens concept and became ubiquitous in DeFi Twitter culture. "GM frens" is a common morning greeting.
G
General

Gas

The unit of computational effort required to execute an Ethereum transaction or smart contract call. Gas is priced in gwei (1 gwei = 10-9 ETH) and paid to validators. Complex DeFi interactions consume more gas than simple transfers.

Dashboard
Gas fees spike during network congestion. DeFi interactions like multi-step swaps or complex vault operations can cost $10–$200+ in gas during peak periods on Ethereum mainnet.
Governance

Governance Token

A token that confers voting rights in a DAO. Token holders can propose and vote on protocol upgrades, parameter changes, treasury allocations, and fee structures. The weight of votes is typically proportional to token holdings.

Curve MakerDAO Aave
Large token holders ("whales") can dominate governance votes. Quorum requirements set the minimum participation needed for a proposal to pass.
H
Lending

Health Factor

A numerical score indicating the solvency of a borrower's position = (Total Collateral × Collateral Factor) / Total Borrowed Value. Below 1.0 triggers liquidation. Higher health factor = safer position.

Aave Compound
If your Health Factor drops below 1.0, your collateral can be liquidated by anyone. Most protocols recommend keeping HF > 2.0 for safety margin against price volatility.
General

Hooked

Slang for being psychologically and financially invested in a DeFi protocol or token community. Once hooked, you're actively checking positions, participating in governance, and accumulating more — frens don't leave.

Dashboard
Protocols use yield farming, NFT rewards, and governance token incentives to make users hooked. The community aspect is often what keeps frens around even through bear markets.
I
AMM

Impermanent Loss (IL)

The difference in value between holding assets in an AMM liquidity pool versus holding them in a wallet. Occurs when the price ratio of pooled assets diverges from deposit-time ratio. Called "impermanent" because it locks in only when LP removes liquidity.

Curve Risk Dashboard
IL is typically most severe in volatile token pairs. Stablecoin/stable pairs (USDC/USDT) have near-zero IL. Impermanent loss is a hidden cost that erodes LP returns before fees.
Risk

Incentive Alignment

The degree to which the incentives of different protocol participants (lenders, borrowers, stakers, team) are aligned to promote behaviour that benefits the protocol long-term rather than exploiting others.

Risk Dashboard
Poor incentive alignment leads to moral hazard — where one party can take risks that are socialised onto others. The best DeFi protocols design game-theoretic incentive structures carefully.
J
MEV

JIT Just-In-Time Liquidity

A MEV strategy where a bot detects a large pending swap in the mempool, front-runs it by providing liquidity just before the swap executes, then withdraws immediately after. Collects extremely high LP fees but requires precise timing and gas optimization.

MEV Curve
JIT was more common before Uniswap V3's range tick mechanism made it structurally similar. It can harm regular LPs by creating extreme price impact then normalizing.
K
MEV

Keeper

An autonomous bot that performs necessary protocol maintenance tasks — liquidating unhealthy positions, triggering protocol actions, or maintaining peg stability. Keepers earn fees for executing these tasks.

MEV MakerDAO
Keepers are the operational backbone of many DeFi protocols. In MakerDAO, keepers bid on ETH collateral at auction. In Aave/Compound, keepers liquidate underwater positions.
L
Staking

Liquid Staking

A staking mechanism that issues a liquid token (LST) representing the user's staked ETH position. LSTs can be used in DeFi while ETH is staked, enabling yield on yield. Prominent examples: Lido stETH, Rocket Pool rETH, Fraxtal frxETH.

Lido EigenLayer
Post-Shanghai upgrade, staked ETH withdrawals are enabled, but liquid staking remains popular for composability. LSTs trade at slight discounts or premiums to spot ETH based on demand.
Lending

Liquidation Bonus

The financial reward paid to liquidators for closing an underwater borrower position. Typically a percentage of the collateral value — e.g., a 10% liquidation bonus means liquidators can buy $1,000 worth of collateral for $900 of borrowed assets.

Aave Compound
A high liquidation bonus can cause cascading liquidations as liquidators compete. Protocols tune this dynamically based on gas costs and market conditions.
Lending

Liquidation

The forced closure of a collateralized borrowing position when its health factor drops below 1.0 due to collateral price decline or borrowed asset price increase. A liquidator repays the debt and receives the collateral at a bonus.

Aave MakerDAO Risk Dashboard
Liquidators are typically automated keeper bots competing for the bonus. Users can avoid liquidation by maintaining a high health factor, adding collateral, or reducing debt.
Staking

Lockup Period

A defined period during which deposited tokens cannot be withdrawn. Used in staking protocols to ensure long-term commitment and prevent governance attacks. Curve uses CRV lockups; EigenLayer uses ETH restaking lockups.

Curve EigenLayer
Longer lockup periods often come with higher yield boosts or governance power multipliers (veCRV model).
AMM

LP Liquidity Provider

A user who deposits token pairs into an AMM liquidity pool to enable trading. LPs earn swap fees proportional to their share of the pool. In return, they receive LP tokens representing their fractional ownership.

Curve Aggregators
LP returns = swap fees earned − impermanent loss − gas costs. The net return can be negative in highly volatile pools even if trading volume is high.
Staking

LSD Liquid Staking Derivative

A token representing a user's stake in a proof-of-stake network, tradeable on secondary markets while the underlying stake remains locked. Examples: stETH (Lido), rETH (Rocket Pool), frxETH (Frax).

Lido EigenLayer
LSDs are one of the most capital-efficient DeFi primitives — they allow ETH to earn staking yield while simultaneously being used as collateral in lending markets.
Lending

LTV Loan-to-Value

The ratio of borrowed value to collateral value, expressed as a percentage. Maximum LTV is set by the protocol and defines the borrowing limit. When LTV exceeds the liquidation threshold, the position is subject to liquidation.

Aave MakerDAO
LTV is the inverse of the collateral factor: a collateral factor of 75% corresponds to a max LTV of 75%. ETH typically has 80% LTV on Aave; wBTC has 70%.
M
MEV

MEV Maximal Extractable Value

The profit a block proposer (miner/validator) or MEV searcher can extract by reordering, front-running, or back-running transactions within a block. MEV was formerly called "Miner Extractable Value" before the Merge.

MEV
MEV is a double-edged sword: it can improve market efficiency through arbitrage but also enables front-running that harms retail traders. The Flashbots ecosystem attempts to democratize MEV rewards.
Risk

Morphology (Risk)

In risk analysis, morphology refers to the structural classification of different DeFi risk types — market risk, credit risk, liquidity risk, operational risk, and governance risk. Understanding morphology helps frame which risks are correlated and which are independent.

Risk Dashboard
A robust risk framework maps all DeFi risks into a morphology tree and identifies single points of failure across the stack.
N
General

Narrative

A thematic investment thesis that captures market attention and drives token price movements independent of fundamentals. Examples: "AI Summer," "Restaking," "Liquid Restaking," "RWA." Narratives can inflate bubble cycles and drive capital flows.

Dashboard
Being early to a narrative is highly profitable. By the time a narrative is fully priced in ("narrative is priced in"), the opportunity has passed.
General

Native Token

The primary cryptocurrency of a blockchain — ETH for Ethereum, MATIC for Polygon, SOL for Solana. Used to pay gas/transaction fees and can serve as collateral or staking asset within that chain's DeFi ecosystem.

Lido
On L2s like Arbitrum and Optimism, the native token (ETH) is used for gas. Some L2s have their own governance tokens (ARB, OP) used for protocol governance.
O
General

Oracle

A data service that feeds external information (primarily asset prices) into on-chain smart contracts. Without oracles, DeFi protocols cannot know the current market price of assets used as collateral. Chainlink is the dominant oracle network.

MakerDAO Aave Risk Dashboard
Oracle manipulation attacks (flash loan price attacks) are a major DeFi exploit vector. Protocols use TWAPs (time-weighted average prices) and multi-oracle setups to mitigate manipulation risk.
P
Staking

Penrose / Curve Wars

The competitive race to accumulate veCRV (vote-escrowed CRV) to control Curve DAO governance and direct CRV emissions to preferred pools. Protocols like Convex Finance and Yearn Finance accumulated large veCRV positions, creating a multi-billion dollar governance battle.

Curve Risk Dashboard
The Curve Wars illustrated how governance token concentration can be a systemic risk — whoever controls CRV emissions controls the largest stablecoin liquidity layer on Ethereum.
Governance

PoH Proof of Humanity

A social identity verification system that uses human verification (KYC + video interview) to assign unique personhood credentials on-chain. Used to prevent Sybil attacks (one person multiple identities) in token distributions and governance.

Governance
Gitcoin Grants uses PoH to prevent duplicate quadratic funding contributions. Worldcoin uses a similar biometric approach with its Orb device.
Lending

Pool Utilization

The percentage of supplied liquidity that has been borrowed at any given time: Utilization = Total Borrows / Total Supply. High utilization (>80%) means tight liquidity, higher borrow rates, and increased risk of insolvency for lenders.

Aave Compound
Interest rate models in lending protocols typically feature a kink point (e.g., 80% utilization) where the borrow rate increases non-linearly to incentivize repayments and attract more supply.
Q
Governance

Quorum

The minimum number of votes required for a governance proposal to be valid. If quorum is not reached, the proposal fails regardless of vote margin. Quorum requirements prevent low-participation governance decisions from having outsized impact.

Curve MakerDAO
MakerDAO requires 50%+ of MKR voted to pass executive votes. Uniswap requires 10M UNI (4% of supply) to bring a proposal to a vote.
R
Staking

Restaking

The practice of re-staking ETH or LSDs (liquid staking derivatives) into additional validation roles to earn additional yield on already-staked capital. EigenLayer pioneered native restaking; Lido allows rETH to be restaked in liquid staking configurations.

EigenLayer Lido
Restaking amplifies yield but also amplifies slashing risk — if an AVS is compromised, restakers can be slashed across all services they're securing simultaneously.
Risk

Risk Profile

A structured assessment of the risks associated with a specific DeFi protocol, asset, or strategy. Risk profiles typically cover smart contract risk, market risk, liquidity risk, oracle risk, and governance risk.

Risk Dashboard
Risk profiles are dynamic — they change as TVL fluctuates, new code is deployed, market conditions shift, and team responses to incidents evolve.
S
MEV

Sandwich Attack

A MEV strategy where a bot front-runs a victim's trade by buying the same asset at a lower price, then sells immediately after the victim's trade executes at the higher price. Highly predatory and profitable for the attacker at the expense of the victim.

MEV Risk Dashboard
Sandwich attacks are most effective against large market orders with high slippage tolerance. Using DEX aggregators with lower slippage settings and MEV protection reduces susceptibility.
Risk

Security Model

The collective mechanisms a protocol uses to protect user funds: smart contract audits (Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, Certik), bug bounty programs, multi-sig timelock wallets, and security councils (like Uniswap's Security Council).

Risk Dashboard
Audits are necessary but not sufficient — they only cover the code at a point in time. Timelocks and security councils provide on-chain upgrade governance that prevents malicious upgrades.
Risk

Shamir Secret Sharing

A cryptographic method of dividing a secret (e.g., a private key) into n shares, requiring k of them to reconstruct the original. Used in multi-sig key management for protocol treasuries to eliminate single points of failure.

Risk Dashboard
If 3-of-5 keyholders hold Shamir shares, any 3 can sign a transaction but no single keyholder or pair can. This dramatically reduces key theft risk.
AMM

Slippage

The difference between the expected execution price of a swap and the actual price at execution. Slippage increases with larger trade sizes and lower liquidity. Set too low, swaps revert; set too high, you're vulnerable to sandwich attacks.

Curve Aggregators Risk Dashboard
A 0.5% slippage tolerance on a $10,000 swap means you accept anywhere from $9,950 to $10,000 value received. For stablecoin swaps, 0.05% slippage is usually sufficient. For volatile tokens, 0.5–1.0% may be needed.
Risk

Smart Contract Audit

A systematic code review by a specialised security firm (Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, Quantstamp, Certik) that identifies vulnerabilities, logic bugs, and potential edge cases before mainnet deployment.

Risk Dashboard
Audits are not guarantees — many major exploits (Beanstalk, Wormhole) occurred in audited code. Always combine audits with bug bounties, timelocks, and on-chain monitoring.
MEV

Sniping

A bot strategy that detects and immediately buys newly listed tokens on a DEX before other buyers can — typically immediately after a liquidity pool goes live. Sniper bots race to be first in line at the initial price.

MEV Risk Dashboard
Sniper bots are highly competitive. They use gas bidding wars to jump the queue. Some DEXs now implement anti-sniping mechanisms like locking LP for the first few blocks.
AMM

Stableswap

An AMM variant optimized for swapping assets that are meant to maintain a 1:1 parity (e.g., USDC/USDT, wBTC/renBTC). Uses a bonding curve that is flat near the peg and more curved at extremes, dramatically reducing impermanent loss for like-valued assets.

Curve
Curve's StableSwap formula allows near-zero slippage for stablecoin swaps — large trades ($10M+) can execute at or near a 1:1 rate. This is impossible on a standard AMM, which would have massive price impact.
Staking

Staking

Depositing a blockchain's native token into a proof-of-stake network to support network operations (validating transactions, securing the chain) in exchange for staking rewards. DeFi staking typically involves LSTs (liquid staking derivatives).

Lido EigenLayer
Staking rewards on Ethereum are approximately 4–5% APY as of 2024, paid in ETH. Liquid staking derivatives allow users to earn staking yields while using their position as DeFi collateral.
Staking

Superfluid Staking

A concept (associated with Superfluid protocol) where token stakes generate streaming yields — rewards that accrue in real-time per second rather than in discrete epochs or periods. Enables continuous, granular yield distribution.

EigenLayer
Superfluid enables use cases like streaming payments, real-time staking yields, and progressive vest schedules where tokens unlock continuously rather than in cliff/vest schedules.
Governance

Sybil Attack

An attack where a single entity creates multiple fake identities (Sybil identities) to gain disproportionate governance power. For example, splitting 1M tokens into 100 wallets of 10K each to meet per-wallet vote caps.

Governance Risk Dashboard
DeFi protocols counter Sybil attacks with identity verification (PoH), per-wallet vote minimums, and quadratic voting mechanisms that make creating many identities disproportionately expensive.
T
Risk

Timelock

A security mechanism that requires a multi-sig transaction to wait a predetermined period (e.g., 48 hours) before executing, giving the community time to detect and respond to potentially malicious upgrades.

Risk Dashboard MakerDAO
Timelocks are standard in major DeFi protocols. A 48-hour timelock means the team cannot instantly upgrade contracts — a malicious upgrade would need to sit publicly visible for 48 hours before activation.
Governance

Treasury

A DAO's stored assets (tokens, NFTs, stablecoins) managed by on-chain governance. Treasuries fund protocol development, grants, security audits, and operational costs. A large treasury indicates protocol health and sustainability.

Curve MakerDAO Aave
MakerDAO's treasury is one of the largest, holding billions in a diversified mix of real-world assets (RWA) and crypto assets. Uniswap DAO holds over $3B in UNI tokens.
General

TVL Total Value Locked

The aggregate US dollar value of all assets deposited in a DeFi protocol. TVL is the primary metric for measuring protocol size and adoption. A protocol with $500M TVL has $500M of user funds at risk in its smart contracts.

Dashboard Risk Dashboard
TVL is reported differently by trackers — some use cross-chain aggregates, others just mainnet. Differences in TVL reporting methodology explain discrepancies between DeFiLlama, DeFiPulse, and DeBank.
General

TVM Total Value Metrics

A broader framework beyond TVL that measures all value flowing through a DeFi protocol — including total swap volume, total loans originated, total governance participation, and other activity-based metrics that give a fuller picture than TVL alone.

Dashboard
TVL can be misleading — a protocol with high TVL may have low usage. TVM captures actual economic activity beyond just deposits.
U
General

UTXO Unspent Transaction Output

Bitcoin's accounting model where each transaction consumes previous outputs and creates new ones. In contrast, Ethereum uses an account-based model. Understanding UTXO vs. account-based models matters for cross-chain bridge design.

Bridges
UTXO's properties make it well-suited for privacy-preserving protocols. zk-rollups and Validiums use UTXO-like models within a ZK proof framework for scalability.
V
Staking

veCRV Vote-Escrowed CRV

CRV tokens locked for up to 4 years in Curve DAO. veCRV holders govern the protocol, vote on gauge weight allocations (deciding which pools get CRV emissions), and earn 50% of Curve's trading fees. Longer lock = more veCRV = more voting power.

Curve
A 4-year lock of 1 CRV = 1 veCRV. A 1-year lock of 1 CRV = 0.25 veCRV. veCRV is non-transferable. The lockup mechanism ensures long-term aligned incentives for Curve governance.
Governance

Vesting

A schedule that unlocks allocated tokens gradually over time rather than all at once. Vesting typically has a cliff (period before any tokens unlock) and a linear or granular unlock schedule. Used to align team, investors, and advisors with long-term protocol success.

Curve Aave
A 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff means no tokens unlock in year 1; then 25% unlocks at year 1; then remaining 75% unlocks monthly or quarterly over the next 3 years. Uniswap's team and investor UNI tokens vest over 4 years with a 1-year cliff.
Risk

Volatility

The degree to which an asset's price fluctuates over time, typically measured as the standard deviation of daily returns. High volatility assets (ETH, MEME tokens) require larger collateral factors and liquidation buffers.

Risk Dashboard Aave
In DeFi lending, volatility directly affects how quickly a borrower's health factor can drop. Assets with >50% daily volatility swings have very low collateral factors (if accepted at all) because price drops can immediately trigger liquidations.
W
Risk

Wallet Diversity

Distributing a DAO's or protocol's signing keys across multiple holders, geographic regions, and security setups to prevent a single point of failure. A 3-of-5 multi-sig is more secure than a 1-of-2 multi-sig.

Risk Dashboard
Wallet diversity is a fundamental security practice. The Ronin bridge hack succeeded because all 5 validation keys were controlled by a single entity (Axie/Coatue). Distributed keys across independent organizations resist targeted attacks.
General

WBTC Wrapped Bitcoin

An ERC-20 token backed 1:1 by Bitcoin held in custodied reserves (via BitGo). Enables Bitcoin holders to access Ethereum DeFi — using BTC as collateral on Aave, supplying to Curve pools, or earning yield in Frax.

Aave Curve Bridges
WBTC is bridged Bitcoin — users trust BitGo's custodianship of the underlying BTC. Alternatives like renBTC (now discontinued) and HBTC offer different custodian models. The wBTC trust model has been scrutinized post-2022.
Y
Lending

Yield Aggregator

A protocol (e.g., Yearn Finance, Beefy Finance) that automatically moves user funds between DeFi strategies to maximimize yield. Depositors get a single vault that optimises across lending protocols, AMMs, and staking positions automatically.

Aggregators Curve
Yearn vaults automate complex multi-step strategies — e.g., USDC → Aave lending + Curve LP + Convex staking — that would be too gas-intensive for individual users to execute manually.
Lending

Yield Farming

The practice of deploying capital across DeFi protocols to maximimize returns by earning token incentives, swap fees, and interest. A yield farmer might supply USDC to Aave, LP the aUSDC in Curve, and stake the LP tokens in Convex — stacking yields from multiple sources.

Aggregators Curve Aave
Yield farming returns consist of: base yield (interest from lending/swap fees) + token incentives (protocol emissions) + compound leverage. In bear markets, token incentives can drop to near-zero, making sustainable base yield critical.
Lending

Yield

The return generated on invested capital, expressed as a percentage per year. In DeFi, yield comes from three sources: lending interest, AMM swap fees, and token incentives. The composition of these sources determines sustainability.

Aave Lido Risk Dashboard
A 15% APY might consist of 3% sustainable base yield + 12% token emissions — the latter vanishes when emissions are reduced. Always ask: "What is the sustainable base yield, excluding token incentives?"
Z
General

ZK-Rollup

A Layer 2 scaling solution that bundles hundreds of transactions into a single on-chain proof verified via zero-knowledge cryptography. ZK-Rollups (zkSync, Starknet, Polygon zkEVM) offer high throughput with Ethereum security guarantees.

Bridges
ZK-Rollups post validity proofs (SNARKs/STARKs) on Ethereum mainnet, meaning anyone can verify the chain state is correct. This makes ZK-Rollups more secure than optimistic rollups, which rely on fraud proof challenges.
